title: How Much Is Manual Work Costing You?
subtitle: 5 questions. 90 seconds. A dollar amount you can't unsee.
captureSubtext: We'll send you the full breakdown with 3 specific automations that would save you the most. We will not use this information to haunt you. (The number itself will do that.)

questions.text: What's your hourly rate? (Or what you pay your team)
questions.subtext: Average across the people doing the repetitive work.
questions.tooltip: If you said 'I don't know,' congratulations — you're paying people an unknown amount to do things a robot could do for $0.003 per execution. That's fine. Everything is fine. 🔥

options.label: $200+/hr
options.subtitle: Your time is expensive and you're wasting it

questions.text: How many hours per week does your team spend on repetitive tasks?
questions.subtext: Copy-paste, data entry, manual follow-up, reformatting, updating spreadsheets...
questions.tooltip: McKinsey found that 60% of occupations have at least 30% automatable tasks. That means almost a third of your team's week is doing robot work at human prices. Let that sink in while you pick your answer.

options.label: 10–20 hours/week
options.subtitle: You're paying for 2 days of robot work per week

options.label: 20+ hours/week
options.subtitle: You don't have a team problem, you have a systems problem

questions.text: How many people on your team do this kind of repetitive work?
questions.subtext: Including yourself if you're doing it too. (You probably are.)
questions.tooltip: Solo operators lose 5-15 hours/week to tasks they could automate. A 5-person team? That's 25-75 hours/week of collective capacity being burned on copy-paste. Multiply by 52 weeks. Now multiply by the hourly rate you just told us. We'll wait.

options.label: 10+ people
options.subtitle: You could fund an automation team with what you're losing

questions.subtext: This helps us give you relevant automation examples.
questions.tooltip: Every industry thinks they're 'different' and that automation won't work for them. Every industry is wrong. We've automated workflows for lawyers, real estate agents, e-commerce stores, creative agencies, and a guy who breeds tropical fish. Automation doesn't care about your industry.

options.label: Legal / Professional Services
options.subtitle: Billable hours being burned on admin

options.label: Real Estate
options.subtitle: Follow-up is everything, and you're dropping the ball

options.label: Creative / Content / Agency
options.subtitle: Too much time producing, not enough time creating

options.label: E-commerce / Retail
options.subtitle: Inventory, orders, customer service — all automatable

questions.text: What's your single biggest time waste?
questions.subtext: If you could wave a wand and eliminate ONE task forever, which would it be?
questions.tooltip: The top 3 answers across all industries: 1) Email follow-up and lead chasing (34%), 2) Data entry and reporting (28%), 3) Content creation and formatting (22%). All three can be automated to near-zero with the right system. The wand exists. It's called n8n.

options.label: Invoicing, billing, admin
options.subtitle: You didn't start a business to do bookkeeping
